Key points
• To understand the nutritional and metabolic origin of eicosanoids, as well as the main aspects of their functions.
• To understand the fundamental biochemical processes involved in platelet aggregation.
• To understand the role of eicosanoids in inﬂammation and immune responses.
• To know the main pathophysiological implications of eicosanoids.
Introduction
Given the complexity of multicellular organisms, good intercellular communication is necessary to regulate metabolism, growth
and other functions of the various organs and tissues. This is a very complex network of signals that is gradually becoming better
understood. Many chemical compounds (e. g. hormones, cytokines and eicosanoids) are involved in intercellular communication.
Alterations in the signaling networks cause diseases as important as cancer and diabetes (Johnson et al., 2020).
Eicosanoids are derivatives of polyunsaturated fatty acids of 20 carbon atoms, especially arachidonic and eicosapentaenoic acids.
